item.stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of a rectangular grid that is $3$ squares tall and $8$ squares wide. He wants the even-or-odd parity of the total number of small squares without multiplying $3 \times 8$.

Which claim correctly decides that parity?

options.A: The total is even, because one side length is even.
options.B: The answer is the tall count $3$.
options.C: The total is odd, because $3$ is odd.
options.D: An even total is what forces the grid to be $3$ by $8$.
